title: Value embeddings on every layer (FLOP-free capacity)
description: has_ve() now returns True for all layers, so value_embeds goes from 6 tables to 12 (25.2M -> 50.3M params, total 71.3M -> 96.5M); nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE/wash: val_bpb 0.987155 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. +0.0009, right at the measured noise floor. The cost model was exactly right and the quality model was wrong. FLOPs/token was literally unchanged (3.460393e8, identical to baseline) because estimate_flops() excludes value_embeds, and the wall-clock cost of 6 extra embedding gathers + scatter-add backwards + 6 more AdamW groups was only 2.7% of tokens (322.4M vs 331.5M; MFU 37.4% vs 38.5%; peak VRAM 33.8GB vs 32.1GB). So 25M extra parameters that cost essentially no compute bought essentially no quality. That is a stronger statement than 'capacity is compute-limited': these params were nearly free and still did not help, so the model is not parameter-starved at all -- it is data/optimization-limited at ~330M tokens. The alternating VE pattern is therefore not a compute compromise, it is at or past the useful amount of value-residual, and giving layer 0 a VE (which the alternating pattern denies it) did not help either. Do not buy more embedding-side capacity; the remaining levers are ones that change what the same parameters compute, e.g. WINDOW_PATTERN or the LR schedule shape.
